history.rationale: Lys119 forms the internal aldimine (Schiff base) with the PLP cofactor in the CBS catalytic core; removing the amine side chain eliminates cofactor anchoring and transaldimination. This should abolish catalysis while leaving the fold largely intact.
Charge reversal at the PLP Schiff-base lysine both removes the catalytic amine and introduces electrostatic repulsion with the PLP phosphate/anionic pocket. Expected complete loss of activity.

G307 sits in a tightly packed loop near the active site; G307S is the classic severe, pyridoxine-nonresponsive homocystinuria allele with essentially undetectable activity. Beta-branched side chain cannot be accommodated at this glycine.
Thr257 in the GTGGT loop hydrogen-bonds the PLP phosphate; substitution with a bulky hydrophobic Met disrupts cofactor positioning. Reported as a severe loss-of-function pathogenic variant.

Thr191 lies in a conserved active-site-proximal segment contacting the PLP/substrate region; T191M is a well-known severe, pyridoxine-nonresponsive mutation with near-null activity. Bulky Met perturbs local packing and cofactor geometry.
Gly259 in the flexible GTGGT phosphate-binding loop requires backbone flexibility and minimal side-chain volume. Adding a side chain should distort PLP phosphate coordination and abolish turnover.

Gly148 is in the highly conserved TSGNT PLP-binding motif of fold-type II PLP enzymes; introducing a large positively charged Arg sterically and electrostatically disrupts the cofactor site. Reported as a severe pathogenic substitution.
Arg336 makes buried salt-bridge/hydrogen-bond contacts stabilizing the catalytic domain; loss to Cys destabilizes the active-site scaffold. Known pathogenic variant with strongly reduced activity.
Glu302 participates in an active-site-proximal electrostatic network; charge reversal is expected to misalign catalytic residues. Reported as a disease-associated, low-activity variant.

Cys52 is the thiolate axial ligand of the regulatory heme; C52S ablates heme ligation and is associated with severe misfolding and greatly reduced activity. Less certain to be fully null than direct PLP-site mutations.
